headline: Miners lift the ASX as Wall Street steadies before Thanksgiving
paragraphs: Mining and energy shares drove the ASX 200 up 0.8% to about 8,763 at Thursday’s Sydney close, reversing Wednesday’s loss. The ABS also reported that private capital spending jumped 12.2% in the September quarter, led by investment in data centres. The spending figures show how strongly that investment is still growing in Australia, even as investors question the price of AI shares in the US.

Wall Street recovered most of a steep early fall on Wednesday in New York. The S&P 500 closed down 0.25% at 7,182.78 and the Nasdaq-100 lost 0.64% to 26,046.90, while the Dow rose 0.33%. The pullback in AI shares and fresh tariff worries kept pressure on the broader market. The US PCE inflation rate rose to 3.8% in October, with core inflation at 3.3%, giving the Fed little reason to ease.

The Australian dollar edged up to 66.35 US cents at 5:43 pm Sydney, 0.09% above MarketWatch’s previous close. That was a small recovery after Wednesday’s inflation reading failed to sustain an early jump. Spot gold went the other way on Thursday: Kitco’s bid was down 0.62% at US$3,565.60 a troy ounce at 5:56 pm Sydney. Higher interest rates make holding gold less attractive because it pays no interest.

Oil extended its rebound. January Brent was US$95.09 a barrel in a delayed 5:17 pm Sydney quote, up 0.51% from Wednesday’s US$94.61 settlement, which had already risen 3.5%. AP reported that worries over Middle East supply continued to support crude. There’s no US cash share session tonight for Thanksgiving; the next New York session closes early at 5 am Saturday Sydney time.
